sources.title: Los Mallos de Riglos: The Steep, Wild, Multipitch Conglomerate of Spain
sources.notes: Destination article; confirms conglomerate towers and approximately 300 routes.

sections.heading: Destination Snapshot
sections.body: Riglos is steep multi-pitch conglomerate on the Mallos de Riglos: huge towers, exposed climbing and a very different feel from Spain's roadside limestone crags.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Destination Snapshot.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
The climbing is centred on the Mallos de Riglos in Aragon, where freestanding conglomerate towers rise directly above the village. This is a destination for exposure, route length and unusual rock texture.

Riglos is not a casual sport-crag stop. Even when routes are equipped, the scale and steepness make the day feel like multi-pitch climbing from the first pitch.

sections.heading: History And Reputation
sections.body: The Mallos have a long reputation as one of Spain's distinctive multi-pitch venues. Their identity comes from the towers themselves: steep, orange-brown conglomerate walls that look improbable until you start reading the holds.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for History And Reputation.

sections.heading: Rock And Climbing Character
sections.body: The rock is conglomerate, with steep walls and pebble holds. Movement can feel gymnastic and three-dimensional, but the exposure is real and the routes are long enough to demand efficient rope work.

sections.heading: Who It Suits
sections.body: Riglos suits confident multi-pitch teams. It is best for climbers who are comfortable with height, route finding, belay transitions and committing terrain.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Who It Suits.

sections.heading: Grades And Scale
sections.body: Current destination coverage describes roughly 300 routes at the Mallos de Riglos. The useful filter is less the total count and more the tower, route length, equipment style and descent.

sections.heading: Season

sections.heading: Gear
sections.body: Choose gear by route. Many teams will want a sport-oriented multi-pitch rack, helmets, descent kit and enough water for exposed sunny walls.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Gear.

sections.heading: Getting There
sections.body: A car is the practical way to reach Riglos and move around the region. Once in the village, the towers are the focus and approaches are part of the multi-pitch day.

sections.heading: Local Tips And Rules
sections.body: Pick routes by aspect and commitment, not just grade. The walls are steep and exposed, and an efficient team will have a much better day than a stronger but disorganized one.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Local Tips And Rules.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Wear helmets and plan descents before leaving the ground. Conglomerate, exposure, long routes and heat can all raise the seriousness quickly.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Riglos sport climbing? It has equipped routes, but the destination is fundamentally multi-pitch.

What is the rock? Conglomerate.

Is it beginner friendly? Not as an independent objective. It is better for experienced multi-pitch climbers or guided teams.
